thesis: Affordable SBOM/VEX compliance (vulnerability impact, VEX/CSAF, SBOM lifecycle) for mid-size software and device makers facing EU Cyber Resilience Act obligations (reporting from Sep 2026, main duties Dec 2027), between free Dependency-Track and quote-only enterprise platforms.

themes.name: Dependency context for vulnerability impact
themes.need: Teams analyzing SBOMs and advisories struggle to tell how a vulnerability affects their product because reports lack dependency hierarchy, parent component, container and vendor advisory context.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Teams on free Dependency-Track lack parent-component, container and vendor-advisory context; commercial tools are enterprise quote-only
Dependency-Track has no vendor-managed cloud with support and no reachability; no affordable hosted upgrade path
Ingesting vendor CSAF advisories to match against SBOMs is missing in common tooling
Transitive dependency graph views only work on some input types (bundled artifacts)

market_research.wtp_evidence: Public AWS Marketplace prices: Interlynk SBOM contracts $18k-$100k by active developers; Anchore Enterprise $34.5k-$50k per 12 months. Manifest signed a three-year device-maker deal (value undisclosed).
market_research.bundling_note: AWS Inspector exports SBOMs free and JFrog/SCA suites add graph views, but cross-vendor VEX/CSAF product-impact analysis is not given away by clouds.
market_research.summary: Real but competitive opening: an affordable hosted SBOM impact/VEX layer (CSAF ingestion, dependency paths, container mapping) for mid-size software and device vendors preparing for CRA's Dec 2027 SBOM duty, between free Dependency-Track and enterprise quote-only platforms.

threat.reason: Dependency context speeds triage of vulnerable or compromised components, an indirect exposure reduction.

paid_market_gaps.gap: Artifact attestations for private repos require GitHub Enterprise Cloud; smaller teams can't tie SBOMs to releases cheaply
Management platforms mostly quote-only; few transparent-priced options for small manufacturers facing CRA SBOM duties
Inspector exports only CycloneDX 1.4; bundled exports lag current CycloneDX spec and VEX
SBOM-based vulnerability management yields noisy results; VEX workflow to suppress false positives remains immature

market_research.wtp_evidence: Public list prices: Anchore Enterprise $34,500-$50,000/year plus $15,000 support plan; Interlynk $18k-$100k/year by active developers; sbomify Business $159/month billed annually.
market_research.bundling_note: GitHub and Docker already bundle SBOM attestations at build, but cross-vendor SBOM/VEX lifecycle management and regulator-facing workflows are not given away by platforms.
market_research.summary: Modest opening: SBOM+VEX lifecycle management for SMB manufacturers facing EU CRA (Dec 2027) and FDA 524B, with transparent pricing. Crowded with funded specialists (Anchore, Manifest, Interlynk); attestation alone is bundled by GitHub/Docker.

threat.reason: SBOM format support and attestations are mostly compliance and interoperability; candidates are unrelated.

flagged_claims.claim: Interlynk pricing: 'free Community tier; AWS Marketplace 12-month SaaS contracts by active developers: $18,000 (10), $36,000 (25), $60,000 (50), $100,000 (100)'; segment 'SMB to enterprise, device makers'
flagged_claims.issue: The listing confirms the four 12-month prices, which are for a product named 'AWS SBOM Manager (SaaS)'. It mentions only a 'free trial', not a free Community tier, so the free tier is unsupported. On buyers, the listing names medical device manufacturers, connected-device and firmware teams, AI providers and '100+ regulated companies'. It says nothing about SMBs.

flagged_claims.claim: WTP: 'Manifest signed a three-year device-maker deal (value undisclosed)' (wtp_source: commission.europa.eu Cyber Resilience Act news, 2026-09-11)
flagged_claims.issue: The cited European Commission page covers only CRA reporting obligations, which start 11 Sep 2026, with main obligations from 11 Dec 2027. It never mentions Manifest or any deal. The Manifest deal is supported only by the PR Newswire release in the vendor row (a three-year SaaS agreement with a publicly traded medical device maker, May 2024, value not disclosed), which is not among the wtp_sources. The cited WTP source does not support this claim.
